# Open questions — legeos

What is not yet known, and what has since been answered.

## Open

### Persisted derived logical ids do not follow grouping-rule improvements once real deployments exist

`open` · `@legeos.question.derived-logical-ids-do-not-follow-rule-changes/1`

Minted logical ids are persisted for stability, so a host that scanned under older grouping rules keeps handing out the old ids after the rules improve (seen with the suite-split fix: a database that fused Cosmic Settings' 32 panels keeps the fused id until wiped or re-scanned). No real deployment ever ran the buggy grouping — only dev-scratch databases — so no reconciliation shipped with the fix. The open policy: when grouping rules change after real deployments exist, what reconciles derived (never user-sourced) rows whose component no longer matches? A one-shot drop of derived rows was drafted and deliberately not landed.

### When ADR-0004's GRUB boot-entry generation lands, who writes legeos.deployment= into the generated entries?

`open` · `@legeos.question.grub-entries-must-carry-the-deployment-id/1`

D2 wired hostd's boot-attempt reconciliation, and systemd-boot entries now carry legeos.deployment=<id> so staged-vs-booted is answerable. The GRUB path depends on its generated entries carrying the same exact-match parameter, which is boot-entry generation work under ADR-0004 (still proposed; D3 deferred). Until that exists, GRUB reconciliation reports CannotTell and counts nothing — strictly better than the previous never-moving counter, but the loop is only closed on systemd-boot. Recorded in distro/deploy/README.md.

### Homegarden: the choices left to the user after Phase 4's day of use

`open` · `@legeos.question.homegarden-open-choices/1`

(1) Should the Desktop tray become an ordinary pinned Place that can be unpinned and recede, instead of a permanent default? (2) May the tender shrink another garden tile to make room (garden-only yield set), or only grow into empty cells? Phase 3 ships garden-only yield. (3) Home corner for first growths: bottom-left, opposite the Files object (shipped default), or beside the Desktop tray? (4) Do the garden.* verbs stay named garden, or become home.pin/home.hide to match home.reveal? (5) The stage thresholds in sessions and garden-hours (Expanded->Tile after 3 later sessions and 6 garden-hours idle, etc.) are illustrative: which values match a working week? Answer after @legeos.work.homegarden-hands-on.

### Nothing on the system bus can hand a file descriptor to a session service, which blocks both candidate index backends

`open` · `@legeos.question.no-route-for-a-privileged-fd-to-reach-the-per-user-daemon/1`

Two independent lanes reached the same wall. A privileged fanotify group opened with FAN_MARK_FILESYSTEM, and a root-owned 0600 btrfs send stream, are both file descriptors that lege-hostd can obtain and lege-filed cannot. But no org.legeos.Host.* interface has a type="h" argument anywhere in interfaces/dbus/, and no zvariant Fd or OwnedFd appears under services/lege-hostd/src/. The only fd-passing precedent in the repository is Files.Index1.OpenSnapshot, which is a per-user session service handing an fd to its own clients, not a privileged system-bus service handing one across the privilege boundary. So: should lege-hostd gain a general, auditable way to pass a restricted fd to a session service, and if so what limits its use — which caller identities may ask, what the fd is allowed to be, and how the receiving daemon proves it did not widen its own privilege by accepting one? Until this is answered, both FAN_MARK_FILESYSTEM and the btrfs delta stream are blocked on transport rather than on merit, and ADR-0003 forbids the obvious shortcut of giving CAP_SYS_ADMIN to the per-user lege-filed.

**Blocks**
- `completed` [Adaptive persistent index maintenance — coverage tiers, split freshness, a watcher that sleeps, and a measured backend choice](ACTIVE-WORK.md#adaptive-persistent-index-maintenance--coverage-tiers-split-freshness-a-watcher-that-sleeps-and-a-measured-backend-choice) `@legeos.work.adaptive-index-maintenance/1`

### An application has no way to report a document becoming dirty outside a pressure event

`open` · `@legeos.question.no-way-to-report-a-document-becoming-dirty/1`

E2 gave unsaved-work claims an expiry and a producer that reports both directions from the checkpoint relay, but the relay only speaks when a checkpoint is requested. The plan's 'sessiond document-dirty producer' needs an application-facing surface that does not exist: Checkpoint1 is application-served and has only Request, and nothing else carries a dirty-document signal. A genuine unsolicited producer needs a new method on Checkpoint1 or a sessiond interface — an interface decision beyond E2's scope. Until then the 10-minute TTL is the safety net.

## Recently closed

### Default field density: every drawer sits at the 2x2 floor, so the resize gesture is inert on first use

`resolved` · `@legeos.question.home-field-default-density/2`

The default field packs its drawer block at the 2x2 widget floor, so every neighbour of a resize is already at minimum span and the clamp rule reduces every grow request to nothing: on the default layout the neighbour-yielding resize does nothing visible. This is correct behaviour under the clamp-rather-than-evict rule the user set, but it makes the foundation's headline gesture look broken the first time anyone tries it. Should the default field keep this density (information-first, all eight drawers visible) and accept that resize only becomes useful once the user removes or shrinks something, or should the default leave slack — fewer drawers, a larger starting span for one or two, or deliberate empty cells — so the resize is discoverable on first use? This is the user's call, not an implementation detail.

**Resolution.** Answered by @legeos.decision.home-field-default-leaves-slack: slack, taken as lower floors rather than fewer drawers, so all eight stay on the field and a roomy one looks unchanged. The call was forced rather than chosen. Adding notifications as a third system widget made the old density unsatisfiable — no arrangement of a 1200x800 field seated three 3x2 system tiles and eight 2x2 drawers while both placing the launcher and keeping every open window visible. This was flagged as the user's call and was taken during an improvement pass authorised as 'any improvement is on the table', with the build otherwise broken. It is worth confirming: if information-first density is preferred over a discoverable resize, the decision record names the two levers.

**Resolved by** [The Home Field's default leaves slack: floors below preferred sizes, and a drawer block bounded by a share of the width](DECISION-HISTORY.md#revision-1--the-home-fields-default-leaves-slack-floors-below-preferred-sizes-and-a-drawer-block-bounded-by-a-share-of-the-width) `@legeos.decision.home-field-default-leaves-slack/1`

### Which version authority reconciles the dev lane's --deb-version with the archive lane's debian/changelog?

`resolved` · `@legeos.question.package-version-authority-across-lanes/2`

The dev deployment lane stamps BuildSetIds via cargo-deb --deb-version, bypassing debian/changelog, while the Stage-2 archive lane builds from debian/changelog. Two version authorities cannot coexist into release: either a changelog entry is generated at release time from the build-set machinery, or debian/rules learns to accept LEGEOS_BUILD_SET so both lanes share one source. This must be settled before the archive.legeos.org lane is finished.

**Resolution.** Resolved 2026-09-03 by @legeos.decision.build-set-id-is-the-version-authority: the BuildSetId is the one authority and the debian/changelog head entry is generated from it at build time. Implemented under @legeos.work.build-set-archive-verification.

**Resolved by** [The BuildSetId is the one version authority; debian/changelog is generated from it](DECISION-HISTORY.md#revision-1--the-buildsetid-is-the-one-version-authority-debianchangelog-is-generated-from-it) `@legeos.decision.build-set-id-is-the-version-authority/1`
